findings.title: Selftest cannot distinguish the two F6(e) readings at the aggregate
findings.detail: The spec now says the runner implements reading 1: a non-default type with no admissible reference is reported and does not fail the aggregate F6e_stack_type_spot_check. Both stack-type scenarios (stack_types and stack_types_nan) plant faults that make the aggregate fail anyway. A runner that fails the aggregate whenever spot_none is non-empty (the alternative reading) therefore still passes the selftest. The code does implement reading 1 (evaluate builds the aggregate from a3s only), but only code inspection shows it.
findings.evidence: Mutant X1: replaced 'ck("F6e_stack_type_spot_check", all(_within(v, g["a3_max"]) for v in a3s.values()),' with '... and not run.spot_none,' and ran it through t0309_mutations.run_mutant. Result: rc 0, 0 FAIL lines (survives).
findings.suggested_check: Add a scenario with no F6(e) plant and one type without an admissible reference, and assert that the aggregate passes.

findings.title: Non-finite guard in _a3_die is tested on the finite-volume side only
findings.detail: The spec says a NaN or infinite Tj in any of the six levels gives A3 = NaN. The only plant (fv_tj_nan) is on a finite-volume level. A guard that checks only the finite-volume values passes the selftest. A NaN on a scikit-fem level would then make mfos.metrics.max_gci_consistency raise and stop evaluate with no F6(e) check written, which is the defect this change claims to fix. It fails closed (a crash), not open.
findings.evidence: Mutant X2: 'vals = [float(v) for v in (*p, *r)]' changed to 'vals = [float(v) for v in r]'. Result: rc 0, 0 FAIL lines (survives). mfos.metrics._finite_rows raises on any non-finite column (metrics.py:93-99).
findings.suggested_check: Plant one NaN Tj on a scikit-fem level of a spot-check reference's reference row and require the per-type value to be NaN.

findings.title: Founder-facing F6(e) choice leaves out the 'before any verdict' wording and the INVALID option
findings.detail: O003 scope_in (objective.yaml:110-114) requires the spot check 'before any verdict' on at least one reference of every non-default stack type. The new founder_decisions entry quotes only part of that sentence and offers two readings: reported/not gated, or FAIL F6e. A third reading, no verdict (INVALID), arguably follows most directly from 'before any verdict', and the spec already uses it elsewhere (the ~416 GB entry: 'E008 gives no verdict (F6e: INVALID)'). The founder is offered a narrower choice than the objective text allows.
findings.evidence: objective.yaml line 110: 'the stack-type spot check required by O007's decision_if_pass and D0013 addendum 2, before any verdict: on at least one reference of every stack type other than C004's default...'
findings.suggested_check: List INVALID / no verdict as a third option in the founder_decisions entry.

findings.title: E008.yaml is hand-edited while make_spec.py claims to be its writer
findings.detail: research/o003/e008_dev/make_spec.py says 'Writes experiments/drafts/E008.yaml ... so the draft cannot carry a hand-typed value'. It still carries the T0305-era F6e description and none of this change's founder_decisions entries. Re-running it would silently drop them. The drift predates this change.
findings.evidence: make_spec.py:317 F6e description lacks the T0308/T0310 text; make_spec.py:394 writes E008.yaml.
findings.suggested_check: Port the spec edits into make_spec.py, or mark it as superseded.

findings.title: Wording errors in the rounding docstring and the NaN-handling text
findings.detail: _sig_nm's docstring says 'a 1 nm or larger difference gives a different one'. With round-half-even, 1.5 nm and 2.5 nm both map to 2. The spec's 'above 1 nm' wording is correct. The text 'NaN or infinite thickness raises: ... the reference stops': in the dev path the whole run stops, because dev_reference is called without a try at e008_run.py:2220. A NaN k does not raise; it becomes the string 'nan' in the signature.
findings.evidence: Scratch probe: _sig_nm(1.5e-9) == _sig_nm(2.5e-9) == 2. 200k random pairs: 0 merges above 1 nm, 0 k merges above 1e-8 relative, 0 splits under x(1+1e-15). format(nan, '.8e') == 'nan'.

findings.title: No test case for a NaN in the per-row energy_balance_max field (disclosed)
findings.detail: The notes say T0310 finding 2 also named the per-row energy_balance_max field and that no test case was added for it because the brief did not ask for one. I could not check this against the T0311 brief, which is not in the repository.

independent_checks_performed: Ran DoD: e008_run.py --selftest (rc 0; stack_types 7 failing checks as planted, stack_types_nan 2 failing, F6e 'all' = nan in both), --verify-freeze (rc 0), the E008.yaml key-presence python check (pass), ruff on the runner (pass), mfos exp check E008 (rc 0), thermal_fem.py sha256 prefix a216d5fe3209bcee (match), mfos gate --fast (exit 0, 'all gates passed').
Runner sha256 6d01aa5c...8342 matches runner_sha256_of_unmutated in t0311_mutations.json.
Re-ran research/o003/e008_dev/t0311_mutations.py to $TMPDIR: all 18 mutants rc 1, unmutated rc 0, as recorded.
Wrote my own mutants: X1 (aggregate fails on spot_none) and X2 (guard on the finite-volume side only) both SURVIVE the selftest.

Recomputed dev stack types from the real layouts via dev_reference: gen2_0 = Al2O3_default_dbc with die_thickness_attach_nm [[180000, 50000]]; 2D_Case_4 = other:a9ad6bbb1af1 with raw die thickness 0.00017999999999999998 m and attach 0.0, as claimed.

Numeric probe of the rounding rule: 200k random thickness pairs more than 1 nm apart never merge; 200k k pairs with relative difference above 1e-8 never merge; x(1+1e-15) never splits thickness or k; NaN thickness raises ValueError; exact half-nm ties can merge at exactly 1 nm difference.
Confirmed E008.dev_rows.json carries no stack_type / other:<hash> values, so the hash change leaves no stale classification.

Read mfos.metrics: gci_capped returns NaN without raising, while max_gci_consistency raises on non-finite input, which confirms the crash the _a3_die guard prevents and that a scikit-fem-side NaN reaches F6(e).
Parsed E008.yaml: the new founder_decisions entries and the F6e description load as intended and match the code.
caveats: Completeness against review T0310 was judged only from the finding numbers the change itself cites; the T0310 review text and the T0311 brief are not in the repository.
The selftest protects the 'not gated' F6(e) reading only partly: an aggregate that also fails on types without an admissible reference goes undetected (mutant X1). The code is correct by inspection.
The 'NaN Tj in any of the six levels gives NaN' guarantee is selftested on the finite-volume levels only; a scikit-fem-side NaN is protected only by code inspection (mutant X2).
The founder-facing F6(e) choice offers two readings; O003's 'before any verdict' wording also supports a third (INVALID / no verdict).
The permission layer blocked some scratch commands, so mutants X3-X6 never ran; only X1 and X2 were run.
The rounding rule can still split two values within float noise of a half-nm (or 9th-digit) boundary; this is disclosed and physically implausible.
Scope is the dev path only; the registered path (full(), loading judged references) is not yet written and not reviewed here.
